_what: Every system in sim/, the document section it implements, the roadmap task it belongs to, and the tests that prove it. The audit page reads this with status.json: a system is shown as built only if every test named here passed on the last run of status.py. A test that is renamed or deleted makes its system read 'missing', never 'built'.

systems.name: Fixed-point arithmetic
systems.what: 64-bit with 32 fractional bits for positions, 32-bit with 16 for angles. No floating point anywhere in the simulation.

systems.name: Angles and trigonometry
systems.what: Angles as a fraction of a turn, sine from a committed table computed in exact decimal arithmetic.

systems.name: Seeded randomness
systems.what: SplitMix64 into xoshiro256++, one stream per subsystem so one subsystem's draws cannot shift another's.

systems.name: The tick and its checksum
systems.what: Six phases in a fixed order; a checksum every tick, one a second kept, sensitive to one unit in the last place.

systems.name: Replay format
systems.what: Commands, never state. A header pinning 24.11's four things, a varint command log, and a four-byte checksum a second, under 2 KB.

systems.name: Golden replays
systems.what: Heists encoded by an earlier build and committed; every build re-simulates them and names the second any divergence starts at.

systems.name: Tile grid
systems.what: Per-tile terrain and continuous positions; 5.2's realm sizes; a fixed north-east-south-west neighbour order.

systems.name: Pathfinding
systems.what: Breadth-first, ties by tile index. Terrain slows the walk and cannot bend the route.

systems.name: Crew control
systems.what: The crew never makes a decision the player did not make: no re-routing, no different door, friends pass through one another.

systems.name: Line of sight
systems.what: Per tile, as 21.12 requires. Feet and eyes are separate properties, as 6.2's fence and fog bank require. The same line from either end. What a guard's cone reaches is drawn from the same rule, tile by tile (21.12).

systems.name: Noise
systems.what: Sound travels along the walkable path, never through walls: a guard turns toward the way around, not toward the source. The document's five carrying distances, in steps a crew would walk.

systems.name: Guard states
systems.what: Unaware, Suspicious, Investigating, Alerted, Searching, Returning, at the document's thresholds. No fall-back inside half a second; ten seconds searching the spot, twenty after losing sight, then home. Nothing random in it: §12.17 promises a scouting player can predict exactly what will happen.

systems.name: Realm alarm
systems.what: An alert reaches guards within four metres half a second later; the realm alarm climbs once every thirty seconds to six, and each level keeps the ones below it: from one suspicion empties at half its rate, from two every noise carries a metre further except a crouched step on moss, from three an Investigating guard searches 20 seconds, from four the alarm and a Lantern Glare reach 8 m, at five one more Warden arrives at the entrance, and at six every guard enters Searching (TD.69). A bell post's ring waits for the bell post (TD.15).

systems.name: Detection modifiers
systems.what: The corner of the eye at half the rate; crouched halves, running adds three quarters, an unlit tile halves again, multiplied once; still in tall grass is invisible until a guard walks into the tile; gravel and water carry sound further, moss less; and the realm's watch (v3.7): suspicion fills at 0.6 at realm level 1, and every zone reaches 0.75 and 0.7 as far at levels 2 and 3.

systems.name: Roles and gaits
systems.what: Crew and guards move at §11.1's speed for their role, over any number of tile edges. Walk, crouch or run by command; the two gait speeds are the simulation's reading, since the document gives neither.

systems.name: The Vault and loading
systems.what: 1,500 health a Vault level, cracked from beside it one hit every 0.8 s, Breakers for double and a quarter more while two or more work it (the assist bonus, v3.3); no guard hears the Vault, as the owner decided (F35): v3.4's hit noise and its call every five seconds of cracking are gone, and a guard beside it still sees the crew. Once open, every crew member loads at 30 a second to the fill the player set, until the bag is full or the exposed share is gone — a full crew in ten seconds. A loaded Carrier walks 15% slower.

systems.name: Fights, knockouts and capture
systems.what: One hit every 0.8 s for Power, on both sides. An ambush on a guard that has not noticed the crew is a two-second takedown and a knockout, whatever the roles (v3.3); a guard that notices first takes an ordinary hit, and an open hit sends it to 1000. A body is seen as a still crew member lying on its tile would be, and can be dragged at crouching speed. A crew member at zero health drops its loot and is caught in ten seconds unless an ally revives it (3 s, a Mender 1.5). A knocked-out guard found by another raises the realm alarm.

systems.name: The skiff, the clock and the outcome
systems.what: The skiff comes to an edge tile in 20 s at the Heart and takes whoever holds the spot; anyone inside when the clock ends is caught. §12.9's four grades from who got out with what. A heist planned as a player would play it ends Clean with every bag full. Loading stops when the clock left no longer covers getting out; dropping loot costs exactly the fraction dropped.

systems.name: Landing
systems.what: The crew lands where the raider chooses: a landing in the input log, at tick 0, puts the whole crew on one open edge tile before any other input of that tick. Guards within 6 tiles of the spot, walked as every sound travels (§12.17), start at 250 of 1,000 suspicion unless it is in fog, darkness or tall grass. Ghost tide returns a knocked-out crew member to the landing spot. A late, second or inland landing is dropped, and the server refuses a heist that never lands. An island needs one open edge tile, and a walkable route from some open edge tile to the Vault; `Island::landings` lists the tiles a crew may choose. The Heart's no-landing rule waits for universes of several realms.

systems.name: Laws and pylons
systems.what: All 48 laws as exact ratios, generated from content/law_effects.json. Each tick the rule sheet is the product of the laws whose pylons stand: speed, sight, suspicion, noise, structure and fight damage, alarm range, the clock, Glass and Stillness. A pylon broken — 600 health, Breakers double — switches its law off from the next tick and earns its page. A replay's rules field is a digest of the laws it was made under. Kinship and Regrowth heal once a second, each with its own parameter (F31); Regrowth heals wards too. v3.4's other rows (§7.3) are parameters as well, so the launch 24 are whole: friction off and a wall's rebound (Frictionless, Bounce), health and speed read by size (Density), a triggered effect landing late (Delay), sight in a moving band (Aurora), a hit's jump (Chain lightning), a stun on touch (Static), Revival's return and swap shapes, the highest applying once (Echoes, Soul swap), touch damage (Thorns) and a cut hedge regrowing (Bloom). Where the document leaves the rule open, the reading is G23's.

systems.name: Resonances and chords
systems.what: §8's four kinds of combination, worked out each tick from the laws whose pylons stand, so a broken pylon silences every one its law was part of. Harmonies strengthen the shared kind of effect on both laws — movement, slowing, damage and stuns, healing and regrowth, returns — by a quarter, and Glow and Hush lengthen light and hiding by their tiles. Dissonances add their unpredictable effect from the heist's own seeded stream: gusts, flicker, wildfire, déjà vu. The twelve signature resonances that ship at launch and all twelve chords each change the rule they name. The laws' notes, the resonance pairs and the chords' notes are generated from content, and the rules version covers them. What each combination costs in stability is the economy's, and where §8 stops short of a rule the reading is G25's.

systems.name: Wards
systems.what: All six of §10.3's wards at level 1, as spec/wards.md reads them: Crystal Wall and Thorn Hedge passive, Static Coil an aura, Gravity Well, Time Snare and Lantern Glare triggered by the first crew member in reach and then resetting. Lantern Glare fires within 2 tiles (v3.3). A ward can be disarmed standing on its tile — fifteen seconds at every level, silent, restarting if the disarmer steps off; the ward's sensor ignores the one on its tile disarming it and fires on anyone else (v3.4), but not on the walk there (G18) — or smashed, loudly, Breakers double.

systems.name: Height
systems.what: §6.2's raised ground, 0 to 3 levels: climbing one needs a ramp, stairs or vines, or Honeycomb or Half gravity; dropping is free and one-way, and is heard — 2 m from one level, 4 m from three. A guard a level up sees a metre further per level; one looking up loses its far zone.

systems.name: Island bundles
systems.what: An island as one canonical encoding, addressed by its SHA-256; refused if it is any other encoding. The fixture realm and a legal example Heart are bundles, and every world is built from one.

systems.name: Publishing rules
systems.what: 5.2's ward limit, guard posts and law slots by realm level, one thing a tile, an open edge tile to land on and at least half of each side open (F51, decided), and 6.1's route to the Vault from some open edge tile with every Crystal Wall standing. A builder edits an island through `Island`'s own methods — ground features, posts, wards, woven laws and their pylons, the Vault — each keeping it an island the format can write, and `check` alone says whether it may be published.

systems.name: Rules version and the validator
systems.what: The rules version is a hash of the law table and this build's behaviour on the golden heists, so it moves by itself; the validator re-simulates a replay on the island and rules its header names and returns the re-simulation's outcome.

systems.name: Eras
systems.what: The week's era, first on the rule sheet (§7.3): The Long Night's shorter sight, Glass Moon's see-through walls, Heavy Stars holding Half gravity down, Wildgrowth's stronger Life laws, Echoing Skies as a Revival source, Static Storm's stronger coil and Quiet Week's longer clock. The era travels in the replay (RBH2, one byte; RBH1 unchanged for none) and the table is in the rules version.
